paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples.
model_annotation: The line chart illustrates the performance of two methods—“ST-ES” and “Random”—in terms of minADE₂₀ (a trajectory prediction error metric, lower is better) as the number of in-context examples increases from 0 to 8. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” is linearly scaled with integer tick marks at 0, 2, 4, 6, and 8. The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (↓),” is linearly scaled from 8.80 to 10.20, with major tick intervals of 0.20. The “ST-ES” method is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers: it begins at approximately 10.22 at 0 examples, drops sharply to 9.18 at 1 example, then gradually declines to 8.86 at 6 examples before slightly rising to 8.88 at 8 examples. The “Random” method is shown as a solid orange line with circular markers: it starts at 9.78 at 0 examples, decreases to 9.58 at 1 example, then fluctuates mildly between 9.46 and 9.56 from 2 to 8 examples, ending at 9.60. Both lines exhibit a general downward trend in error with increasing examples, though ST-ES achieves substantially lower error values across all points.
